title: Scenario-Based Budget Ramp and Contingency Guidelines
author: Monica Alvarez
content:
Purpose
This document defines Redwood Inference's operational guidance for building scenario-based budget ramps, aligning procurement and contract commitments with forecast scenarios, and executing contingency controls for revenue recognition and billing events. The goal is to provide a repeatable framework teams can use to translate product/usage signals into finance actions while minimizing surprise impacts to cash, committed capacity, and revrec timing.

Scope
Applies to: finance, product managers, commercial operations, procurement, legal, and engineering leads who own capacity or purchasing decisions. Covers: quarterly and annual forecasting cadence, intra-quarter model updates, procurement gating for reserved capacity, and recognition/billing triggers tied to contract terms. Does not replace formal contract review with legal or the revenue recognition policy in revrec-and-billing.

Key definitions
- Budget ramp: planned change in spend (opEx or committed CapEx) from one fiscal period to the next tied to growth scenarios.
- Contingency wallet: a short-term reallocation of operating funds reserved for urgent capacity or contract coverage.
- Trigger event: measured condition (metric or date) that requires a pre-defined finance action.

Overview of the scenario approach
1) Baseline (Base case): best-estimate forecast built from current ARR/usage, average ticket size, and trend smoothing over the trailing 12 weeks. Used for monthly operating liquidity and headcount planning.
2) Accelerated growth (Upside): 20–60% higher usage across one or more products; used to size fast-follow capacity, temporary burst pool, and short-term procurement approvals.
3) Contraction (Downside): 15–40% lower usage; used to identify reducible discretionary spend and deferred capacity commitments.
4) Stress (Adverse): 40%+ deviation or major contract churn event; triggers immediate executive review and formal contingency actions.

Assumptions and inputs (what teams must provide)
- Product leads: projected monthly active usage and feature launch dates impacting token volumes.
- Commercial: pipeline coverage and likely conversion windows by cohort.
- Eng infra: lead time on GPU capacity (typical procurement + deployment = 8–12 weeks for dedicated pools; 1–3 days for hosted autoscale changes).
- Procurement/legal: minimum notice periods and penalty clauses in supplier agreements.
- Finance: unit economics assumptions (cost/token, amortization windows for reserved capacity, and recognition windows).

Example thresholds and trigger matrix
- Green: +/- 10% of Base — no action, update forecast at next monthly cadence.
- Amber: +/- 10–30% — Finance & Product triage; if Upside, provision 25% of projected burst capacity in a contingency wallet; if Downside, pause discretionary hire and freeze non-critical procurement.
- Red: >30% deviation or contractual breach risk — Exec review within 48 hours; possible re-negotiation of capacity commitments and initiation of revenue recognition impact assessment.

Procurement alignment and gating rules
1) Local purchases (< $15k): follow standard procurement workflow and do not require scenario approval.
2) Medium purchases ($15k–$150k): require finance sign-off against the current Base and Upside scenarios; include a clause for adjustable delivery dates where possible.
3) Large/committed purchases (>$150k or multi-month GPU pool reservations): must be approved by VP Finance and Head of Engineering and accompanied by a scenario exposure statement.
4) Reserved capacity clause check: procurement must flag any multi-quarter commitments with early termination penalties and notify finance for revrec modeling.

Contract clauses to watch (procurement & legal checklist)
- Billing cadence vs performance window: confirm the invoice schedule and the service delivery window to align with revrec rules.
- Capacity overprovisioning: seek proportional billing clauses (pay-for-usage over baseline) or negotiated credits for idle reserved units.
- Force majeure and termination rights: ensure negotiated notice periods match operational lead times.
- Auto-renew and evergreen clauses: procurement must prevent unintentional rollovers without a 60-day notice to finance.

Revenue recognition and billing policy alignment guidance
- For reserved capacity with upfront payments: finance must evaluate whether payments meet ASC revenue criteria for deferred revenue or should be amortized over the delivery period. Attach a one-line summary to any purchase request >$150k indicating expected revrec treatment (deferred / recognized upon delivery / hybrid).
- For usage-based billing with volume discounts: include modeled discount tiers in the forecast scenario matrix and document the recognition impact for each tier.
- Contract amendments: any amendment that materially changes term or price must be tagged in the CRM and trigger a revrec review within 5 business days.

Monthly operational checklist (minimum required actions)
1) Finance: refresh Base/Up/Down scenarios with latest trailing 12-week consumption and AR cadence.
2) Product: submit any new launches or deprecations with expected token delta.
3) Procurement: surface any near-term renewals (>30 days until renewal) with exposure notes.
4) Legal: confirm any change to notice periods or penalties in active negotiations.
5) Execs: review Amber/Red triggers and sign off on contingency draws.

Contingency wallet governance
- Size: typically 3–8% of quarterly operating budget, adjustable by exec decision.
- Use cases: emergency burst GPUs, one-off credits to customers to prevent churn, bridging early vendor invoices.
- Approval flow: pull requests up to $50k approved by Head of Finance; $50k–$250k requires VP Finance; >$250k requires CFO and CEO.
- Replenishment: wallet replenished on the next monthly close if Base scenario is met or earlier if approved by CFO.

Decision matrix example (tabular view)
Event | Immediate owner | Default action | Documentation required
--- | --- | --- | ---
Upside +25% sustained for 2+ weeks | Product + Finance | Allocate burst pool; open procurement ticket for transient GPUs | Usage report, PO request, contingency draw memo
Downside -20% for 1 month | Finance + People Ops | Freeze hiring and non-essential spend | Revenue forecast revision, hiring freeze notice
Supplier contract with early termination penalty | Procurement + Legal | Negotiate penalty reduction or credit | Contract redline summary, financial exposure calc

Forecast ingestion example (YAML)
forecast_period: 2026-Q1
models:
  - name: base
    metrics:
      expected_tokens: 1,200,000
      average_ticket: 0.0025
  - name: upside
    metrics:
      expected_tokens: 1,600,000
      average_ticket: 0.0022
  - name: downside
    metrics:
      expected_tokens: 900,000
      average_ticket: 0.0030

Runbook: urgent funding request for capacity (<= 72 hours)
1) Product files emergency capacity request in procurement portal with supporting usage spike data and estimated cost.
2) Finance validates unit economics and authorizes contingency draw in writing.
3) Procurement issues expedited PO and confirms vendor lead time and billing milestone.
4) Legal confirms no contract clauses prevent fast-start invoicing and documents any temporary amendment.
5) Engineering stands up burst capacity and provides completion notice to Finance for revrec alignment.

Owner and cadence
- Primary owner: VP Finance (overall governance and approval ladder).
- Secondary owners: Head of Procurement, Head of Product, Head of Engineering.
- Review cadence: monthly operational check-in; quarterly executive scenario review aligned with board materials.

Reporting and artifacts to attach to approvals
- Scenario exposure summary (one page): quantifies Base/Upside/Downside cash and revrec impact.
- Procurement exposure ledger: active commitments, renewal dates, penalty windows.
- Revrec quick memo: expected recognition treatment and timing for any >$150k commitments.

Appendix A — Example approval email template (for contingency draw)
Subject: Contingency Draw Request — Q1 Burst GPUs — $75,000
Recipients: VP Finance, Head of Procurement, Head of Product
Body:
- Summary: Sudden 35% token increase on Search product; request $75k from contingency wallet to provision 120 transient GPUs for 4 weeks.
- Supporting data: link to usage dashboard, expected incremental revenue, mitigation plan.
- Approvals requested: VP Finance signoff (Y/N), expedited PO approval by Procurement (Y/N).

Appendix B — Quick checklist for product launches with procurement impact
- Flag launch at least 8 weeks before go-live if expected reserved capacity is needed.
- Provide token/day estimate and expected first 90-day ramp.
- Present fallback to lower-capacity model variants and expected quality delta.
